records.claim: The scoreboard update and aging algorithm is triggered at decode, execution completion, and instruction decode tick.
records.quote: At decode, an instruction that writes a register stores its ROB index as a tag in the corresponding entry and clears the valid bit. When the instruction completes, we overwrite the payload with the digest of the produced value and set the valid bit.
records.why: The paper explicitly names decode and instruction completion as the events that update register entries, while invalidation occurs as subsequent instructions decode.

records.claim: At instruction decode, an instruction writing a destination register clears the valid bit and stores its ROB index as a 14-bit tag in the payload.
records.quote: At decode, an instruction that writes a register stores its ROB index as a tag in the corresponding entry and clears the valid bit.
records.why: This directly matches the on_decode pseudocode setting valid to 0 and storing the ROB tag.

records.claim: On each instruction decoded, the decay counter of each valid register entry decrements and the entry is invalidated when the counter reaches zero.
records.quote: RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: The countdown of an 8-bit counter from 255 to 0 on each decoded instruction implements invalidation after 256 decoded instructions.

records.claim: When an instruction completes execution matching the in-flight ROB tag, the payload is overwritten with the produced register value digest, valid is set to 1, and the decay counter is initialized.
records.quote: When the instruction completes, we overwrite the payload with the digest of the produced value and set the valid bit.
records.why: This confirms the state transition in on_execution_complete setting payload to the digest and valid to 1.

records.claim: On misprediction pipeline recovery, in-flight register tags younger than the recovery ROB tag are flushed while completed registers retain valid digests.
records.quote: recovering the Tomasulo-like table may present some challenges; we plan to address these in future work.
records.why: The authors state that recovering the Tomasulo-like table on mispredictions is left to future work, leaving the exact squash recovery logic unstated.
records.open_question: How should squashed in-flight registers (with valid=0) in the Tomasulo-like table be recovered upon a branch misprediction squash?

records.claim: The helper function generate_digest(reg_type, value) computes a 12-bit register value digest based on register type as required by on_execution_complete.
records.quote: Figure 6 shows the method we propose for generating digests of register values. RUNLTS generates a 12-bit digest from each 64-bit register value, with the format depending on the register type.
records.why: The paper specifies how digests are generated across register types in Figure 6, but the spec called generate_digest without defining it in any algorithm.

records.claim: Invalidation after 256 decoded instructions ensures only fresh, correlated values influence branch predictions.
